newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares mixed on index-linked sales.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares mixed on index-linked sales.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed at noon on Wednesday as institutions took profits on index-linked counters after a brief buying spree on Tuesday.
There was demand for smaller capitalisation and Malaysian issues, but even this was fairly tame, dealer said.
"People are testing the market. They have their toes in the water but they're not going in," a local brokerage dealer said.
At the lunch break, the Straits Times Industrials Index sank further to 1,996.46, down 7.80 points.
Volume was a mere 35.7 million shares with losers slightly ahead of gainers at 114 to 109.
Dealers said the downtrend was likely to resume now that the psychological barrier of 2,000 points, breached late Tuesday, failed to hold.

SPH foreign fell Singapore 30 cents to S$28.30 on profit taking after a sharp rise on Tuesday. City Development also came off 30 cents to S$13.40 and Van Der Horst and warrants fell 18 cents to S$3.12 and 30 cents to S$2 respectively.
Demand for Malaysian issues was mostly subdued, led by Renong Bhd and warrants, up six cents to S$1.89 and one half cent to S$0.80 respectively.
